::: {#exm-mcmc}
#### A sequence that converges to the standard Gaussian

Let $\theta^{(t+1)} = 0.5\,\theta^{(t)} + \varepsilon_t$,
with $\varepsilon_t \siid \ndist{0, 0.75}$ independent of the past.
Each draw depends on the previous one.
If $\theta^{(t)}$ has mean $m_t$ and variance $v_t$,
then $m_{t+1} = 0.5\, m_t$ and $v_{t+1} = 0.25\, v_t + 0.75$,
so from any starting value $m_t \to 0$ and $v_t \to 1$:
the draws' distribution converges to $\ndist{0, 1}$.
This sequence is an MCMC method for sampling the standard Gaussian distribution;
its draws are correlated, unlike independent draws.
:::
